findings.proposed: Replace the two frozen literal arrays with a data-driven manifest. Add `repos.json` at the workspace root (sibling of the Makefile), shape: {"schema_version": 1, "githubOrg": "DEFRA", "repos": [{"name": "trade-imports-animals-frontend", "stack": "node", "unitTestExempt": false, "alias": "frontend"}, ...]}. repos.js then reads and validates it once against the resolved workspace root and derives NODE_REPOS / JAVA_REPOS / REPOS / UNIT_TEST_EXEMPT_REPOS from it, keeping the current arrays only as the fallback when no manifest is present. Keep the exported names and shapes so every caller (setup, status, clean, install, lint, test, update, reset, branch) is untouched.
findings.why: The repo inventory is the one place where a generic workspace CLI still hardcodes one commodity line's aggregate. A workspace at trade-imports-workspace that aggregates a different set of sub-repos cannot be served without shipping a new tim. A manifest owned by the workspace, not by the CLI, is the natural home — it also lets `make` and the bash tools in tools/ read the same list.
